# MHCS Core — Member-Facing UI Language Policy

## Purpose

This document defines the approved language, terminology, tone, and content-design rules for member-facing and publicly visible MHCS Core interfaces.

It applies to:

* the Member Portal;
* public booking flows;
* member onboarding;
* member notifications;
* member email and SMS content;
* member-facing result pages;
* member help content;
* public queue displays;
* public signage generated by MHCS;
* member-visible operator screens;
* downloadable member documents; and
* product marketing copy that describes the MHCS service journey.

This document governs visible product language. It does not redefine the underlying clinical, technical, legal, operational, or interoperability domain.

## Language requirement

The primary language of all member-facing and publicly visible MHCS interfaces is **Bahasa Indonesia**.

Member-facing UI must not default to English.

This includes:

* page titles;
* navigation;
* buttons;
* form labels;
* form instructions;
* validation messages;
* statuses;
* notifications;
* empty states;
* confirmation messages;
* error messages;
* queue destinations;
* onboarding;
* help content;
* result explanations; and
* plain-language consent explanations shown alongside formal consent text.

English may remain only where it is:

* part of an official product name;
* an established technical standard;
* a file format;
* an unavoidable external term;
* legally required;
* supplied by a third party and required to remain unchanged; or
* more widely understood than an artificial translation.

Examples of terms that may remain unchanged where relevant:

* PDF
* OTP
* DICOM
* FHIR
* NPZ

Technical terms shown to members must be explained in Bahasa Indonesia when they affect understanding, consent, safety, or required action.

## Product language position

MHCS should present radiography as an accessible and structured health service rather than framing every member as a sick patient.

The member-facing experience should emphasize:

* health awareness;
* clear preparation;
* scheduled service;
* professional handling;
* structured history;
* access to results;
* professional review when selected;
* responsible follow-up; and
* continuity between sessions.

The interface must remain accurate and must not imply that radiography alone proves complete health or the absence of disease.

## Default audience terminology

Use **member** as the product and business term for a person using MHCS.

In Bahasa Indonesia UI, prefer:

* Anda
* Member
* Anggota, only where it fits the established product language

Prefer direct second-person language over repeatedly naming the user.

Examples:

* “Jadwal Anda”
* “Hasil sesi Anda”
* “Lengkapi persiapan sebelum sesi.”
* “Laporan dokter sudah tersedia.”

Avoid in ordinary member-facing UI:

* pasien;
* penderita;
* kasus;
* orang sakit; and
* subjek pemeriksaan.

The word **pasien** may remain where required by:

* formal clinical documents;
* doctor-authored reports;
* legal requirements;
* regulated consent;
* external healthcare contracts;
* interoperability standards; or
* terminology supplied by an authorized third party.

Do not change legally or clinically required terminology merely to make it sound friendlier.

## Primary service terminology

The primary member-facing name for the radiography activity is:

**Sesi Foto Radiografi**

Use this term consistently across member-facing and public surfaces.

Preferred examples:

* Sesi Foto Radiografi Baru
* Jadwal Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Persiapan Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Detail Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Hasil Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang
* Antrean Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Sesi Foto Radiografi Selesai

Do not use the following as the default member-facing service name:

* Pemeriksaan Radiologi
* Pemeriksaan Radiografi
* Sesi Pencitraan
* Pemeriksaan Baru
* Sesi X-ray
* Foto X-ray

Formal clinical or technical documents may retain more precise terminology where required.

## Radiography terminology model

Use the following distinction consistently.

### Sesi Foto Radiografi

Use for the complete service activity or member journey.

Examples:

* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Anda dijadwalkan besok.”
* “Pilih lokasi untuk Sesi Foto Radiografi.”
* “Lihat riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi Anda.”

### Foto Radiografi

Use for an individual visible radiographic result or member-accessible image.

Examples:

* “Foto radiografi sudah tersedia.”
* “Buka foto radiografi.”
* “Unduh foto radiografi.”

### Gambar Radiografi

Use for processing, submission, technical quality, or a collection of images.

Examples:

* “Gambar radiografi sedang diproses.”
* “Kualitas gambar radiografi belum memadai.”
* “Sebagian gambar radiografi perlu diambil kembali.”

Do not use these three terms interchangeably when the distinction affects member understanding.

## Use of the term “X-ray”

MHCS-authored member-facing and publicly visible UI copy must not use the term **X-ray**.

Use the approved radiography terminology instead:

* Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Foto Radiografi
* Gambar Radiografi
* Proses Radiografi
* Ruang Foto Radiografi
* Operator Radiografi

This rule applies to MHCS-authored content in:

* the Member Portal;
* public queue displays;
* member booking screens;
* member notifications;
* email and SMS messages;
* member-facing help content;
* marketing pages;
* result summaries;
* public signs;
* member-visible status labels; and
* member-visible portions of operator workflows.

This rule does not authorize modification of:

* signed doctor reports;
* regulated consent;
* legally mandated wording;
* formal clinical records;
* external clinical documents;
* vendor content;
* third-party content required to remain verbatim; or
* interoperability payloads.

Preserve such content unchanged.

Where permitted, provide a separate Bahasa Indonesia explanation using the approved radiography terminology.

The term **X-ray** may remain in:

* internal technical documentation;
* source code identifiers;
* legacy integration contracts;
* device configuration;
* vendor terminology;
* technical protocols;
* professional-only operational screens;
* migration code;
* test fixtures; or
* external material that must remain unmodified.

Internal terminology must not leak into MHCS-authored member-facing output.

## Examination terminology

The word **pemeriksaan** is not globally prohibited.

It may be used when it is familiar, accurate, and limited to a clearly defined activity.

The approved name for the initial operational stage is:

**Pemeriksaan Dasar**

This term refers to the initial collection of basic measurements and health information.

Approved examples:

* Pemeriksaan Dasar
* Menunggu Pemeriksaan Dasar
* Pemeriksaan Dasar Sedang Berlangsung
* Pemeriksaan Dasar Selesai
* Hasil Pemeriksaan Dasar
* Data Pemeriksaan Dasar

Do not replace **Sesi Foto Radiografi** with a generic “pemeriksaan” label when referring to the radiography service.

## Public queue terminology

The approved public queue destinations are:

* **PEMERIKSAAN DASAR**
* **SESI FOTO RADIOGRAFI**

These labels must remain consistent across:

* the public LCD display;
* printed operational signs;
* public calling destinations;
* operator call actions visible to members; and
* recent-call history shown publicly.

Public queue displays must not show:

* member name;
* NIK;
* medical-record identifier;
* booking details;
* health information;
* image information;
* result information;
* waiting-list position; or
* other personal or clinical data.

Ticket number, destination, and call time may be displayed according to the approved queue design.

## Member journey terminology

Use the following member-facing journey where applicable:

1. Pendaftaran dan Verifikasi
2. Pemeriksaan Dasar
3. Sesi Foto Radiografi
4. Pemrosesan Gambar Radiografi
5. Hasil Tersedia
6. Peninjauan Dokter, when the member selected a doctor service
7. Tindak Lanjut, when applicable

Do not describe every stage as a medical examination.

## Internal and member-facing terminology boundary

Do not rename backend models, database concepts, events, FHIR resources, or clinical workflow concepts solely to match member-facing copy.

Internal concepts may include:

* `Member`
* `Booking`
* `Examination`
* `ImagingStudy`
* `ImagingSeries`
* `Radiograph`
* `DiagnosticReport`
* `ClinicalDecision`
* `QualityDecision`
* `RepeatRequest`
* `ConsentRecord`
* `AuditEvent`
* `FhirResource`

The visible UI may map these concepts to simpler member-facing labels.

Examples:

| Internal concept   | Member-facing label                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `Examination`      | Sesi Foto Radiografi                  |
| `ImagingStudy`     | Hasil Sesi Foto Radiografi            |
| `Radiograph`       | Foto Radiografi                       |
| `DiagnosticReport` | Laporan Dokter                        |
| `QualityDecision`  | Penilaian Kualitas Gambar             |
| `RepeatRequest`    | Permintaan Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang |
| `repeat_required`  | Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang Diperlukan |
| `awaiting_review`  | Menunggu Peninjauan Dokter            |

The presentation layer must not change stored domain meaning.

## Tone principles

Member-facing MHCS language must be:

* calm;
* clear;
* preventive;
* professional;
* precise;
* human; and
* non-judgmental.

### Calm

Use composed wording.

Avoid unnecessary alarm, dramatic language, or vague threats.

Preferred:

* “Ada catatan yang perlu ditindaklanjuti.”
* “Baca rekomendasi dokter untuk langkah berikutnya.”

Avoid:

* “Hasil Anda bermasalah.”
* “Ada sesuatu yang berbahaya.”
* “Segera bertindak sebelum terlambat.”

Urgency must still be explicit when clinically required.

### Preventive

Emphasize awareness, monitoring, structured records, and informed follow-up.

Do not promise prevention or guaranteed early detection.

Preferred:

* “Simpan riwayat sesi untuk memantau perubahan dari waktu ke waktu.”

Avoid:

* “Cegah penyakit dengan melakukan radiografi secara rutin.”
* “Pastikan tubuh Anda selalu sehat.”

### Professional

Use credible and direct language.

Avoid:

* jokes;
* playful medical metaphors;
* slang;
* exaggerated reassurance;
* sensational wording; and
* language that trivializes radiation or clinical findings.

### Human

Tell the member what is happening and what they can do next.

Preferred:

* “Gambar radiografi sedang diproses. Anda akan menerima pemberitahuan saat hasil tersedia.”

Avoid:

* “Processing.”
* “Request pending.”
* “Data sedang diproses oleh sistem.”

### Precise

Distinguish materially different states.

Do not merge:

* recommended and required;
* pending and failed;
* processing and professional review;
* no immediate follow-up and no health risk;
* image-quality failure and clinical findings; or
* preliminary and final results.

### Non-judgmental

Do not blame members for:

* incomplete preparation;
* missed appointments;
* unsuccessful image capture;
* required repeat sessions;
* delayed responses; or
* declined optional steps.

Preferred:

* “Sebagian gambar perlu diambil kembali agar dapat ditinjau dengan baik.”

Avoid:

* “Anda gagal dalam pemeriksaan.”
* “Member tidak kooperatif.”
* “Hasil Anda buruk.”

Operational responsibility may be recorded internally in audit data without being exposed as accusatory member-facing copy.

## Safety and transparency

Friendly language must not conceal material safety information.

Member-facing safety content must clearly explain:

* that radiography uses ionizing radiation;
* relevant preparation requirements;
* pregnancy-related questions;
* relevant contraindications;
* expected benefits;
* material risks;
* consent;
* limitations of the service; and
* when professional assistance is required.

Approved example:

“Sesi Foto Radiografi menggunakan radiasi pengion untuk menghasilkan gambar pada bagian tubuh yang dipilih.”

Approved example:

“Beri tahu operator apabila Anda sedang hamil, mungkin hamil, atau memiliki kondisi yang perlu dipertimbangkan sebelum sesi.”

Avoid vague descriptions such as:

* “Teknologi foto modern”
* “Pemindaian kesehatan biasa”
* “Foto tubuh”
* “Proses tanpa risiko”

Do not state that radiation has no risk.

## Consent language

Consent is a controlled safety and legal surface.

Rules:

* use explicit language;
* explain the nature of radiography;
* mention ionizing radiation where relevant;
* do not mix consent with marketing;
* do not preselect consent;
* explain the consequence of declining;
* state whether and how consent may be withdrawn;
* preserve legally required text;
* provide plain-language explanation alongside formal wording where allowed;
* record the consent version, actor, and timestamp according to system requirements; and
* do not rewrite regulated consent without authorized review.

The member-friendly language policy does not override approved consent requirements.

If formal consent contains terminology that differs from this policy, preserve the formal text unchanged and provide a separate explanation where permitted.

## Health-claim boundaries

Never claim or imply:

* “Anda sehat sepenuhnya.”
* “Anda bebas penyakit.”
* “Hasil ini membuktikan bahwa Anda sehat.”
* “Tidak ada risiko kesehatan.”
* “Anda tidak perlu berkonsultasi dengan dokter.”
* “Radiografi ini memeriksa seluruh kondisi tubuh.”
* “Tidak ada temuan berarti tidak ada penyakit.”
* “Foto yang jelas berarti tubuh sehat.”
* “MHCS mencegah penyakit.”
* “Radiografi berkala menjamin deteksi dini.”
* “Hasil ini sepenuhnya normal.”
* “Tidak ada kemungkinan masalah lain.”

Preferred alternatives:

* “Tidak ada catatan khusus pada sesi ini.”
* “Tidak ada hal yang memerlukan tindak lanjut segera pada hasil ini.”
* “Hasil sesi telah tersedia.”
* “Tidak ada temuan akut yang disebutkan dalam laporan dokter.”
* “Pantau kembali sesuai rekomendasi.”
* “Hasil ini membahas bagian tubuh yang dinilai dalam sesi ini.”
* “Hubungi tenaga kesehatan apabila Anda memiliki gejala atau kekhawatiran.”

A limited radiography result must not be converted into a statement about complete health.

## Formal report and member summary

Where MHCS shows both simplified and formal content, clearly separate them.

Recommended structure:

### Ringkasan untuk Anda

A plain-language explanation based on approved structured content or reviewed copy.

### Laporan Dokter

The authoritative formal report.

Rules:

* do not alter signed doctor text;
* do not hide the formal report when the member is entitled to access it;
* do not present automated text as doctor-authored unless it was reviewed and approved;
* clearly label automated explanations;
* preserve uncertainty and limitations;
* preserve recommendations and urgency;
* do not omit clinically material qualifiers;
* do not replace the terminology inside the formal report solely to comply with member-facing terminology; and
* advise professional discussion when a safe simplification is not possible.

Use the following default member-facing status labels only where they match actual domain states.

### Scheduling

* Belum Dijadwalkan
* Menunggu Konfirmasi
* Sesi Foto Radiografi Terjadwal
* Jadwal Diperbarui
* Dijadwalkan Ulang
* Sesi Dibatalkan

### Preparation

* Siap untuk Sesi
* Informasi Tambahan Diperlukan
* Persetujuan Belum Diberikan

### Basic examination

* Menunggu Pemeriksaan Dasar
* Pemeriksaan Dasar Sedang Berlangsung
* Pemeriksaan Dasar Selesai
* Informasi Tambahan Diperlukan

### Radiography session

* Menunggu Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Sesi Foto Radiografi Sedang Berlangsung
* Pengambilan Gambar Selesai
* Gambar Radiografi Sedang Diproses
* Pemrosesan Gambar Selesai

### Professional review

* Menunggu Peninjauan
* Sedang Ditinjau Dokter
* Informasi Tambahan Diperlukan

* Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang Diperlukan

### Follow-up

* Tidak Ada Tindak Lanjut Segera
* Tindak Lanjut Disarankan
* Tindak Lanjut Diperlukan
* Perlu Dibahas dengan Dokter
* Tindak Lanjut Segera Disarankan

Do not use **aman** as a substitute for a clinically scoped outcome.

## Recommended and required actions

The UI must distinguish recommendations from requirements.

Use:

* **Disarankan**, when the action remains optional
* **Diperlukan**, when the workflow cannot continue without the action
* **Harus**, only when a direct safety or legal requirement justifies it
* **Segera**, only when urgency is genuine

Examples:

* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang Disarankan”
* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang Diperlukan”
* “Tindak Lanjut Disarankan”
* “Tindak Lanjut Segera Disarankan”

Do not use softer wording when the action is mandatory.

Do not use mandatory wording when the action is optional.

## Repeat-session language

A repeat session must not sound like member failure.

Preferred:

* “Sebagian gambar radiografi perlu diambil kembali agar dapat ditinjau dengan baik.”
* “Kualitas gambar radiografi belum memadai untuk peninjauan.”
* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang diperlukan untuk melengkapi hasil.”
* “Tim kami akan membantu Anda mengatur sesi ulang.”
* “Sesi ulang disarankan untuk mendapatkan gambar yang lebih jelas.”

Do not promise that a repeat session is free unless the current verified business rules guarantee it.

Avoid:

* “Pemeriksaan Anda gagal.”
* “Foto Anda ditolak.”
* “Hasil Anda buruk.”
* “Kesalahan pasien.”
* “Member tidak kooperatif.”

unless the applicable approved product requirement explicitly requires formal clinical terminology.

## Button conventions

Buttons must describe the immediate action.

Preferred:

* Jadwalkan Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Pilih Jadwal
* Konfirmasi Jadwal
* Lengkapi Persiapan
* Berikan Persetujuan
* Lihat Detail Sesi
* Lihat Foto Radiografi
* Lihat Hasil
* Baca Laporan Dokter
* Unduh Laporan
* Hubungi Bantuan
* Jadwalkan Sesi Ulang
* Lihat Rekomendasi

Avoid vague button labels:

* Lanjut
* Proses
* Submit
* Klik di Sini
* Ya
* Oke

A generic label may be used only when the surrounding context makes the action unambiguous.

For sensitive or destructive actions, use explicit labels:

* Batalkan Sesi
* Hapus Dokumen
* Cabut Persetujuan
* Keluar dari Akun

## Page-title conventions

Preferred titles:

* Sesi Foto Radiografi Baru
* Jadwal Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Persiapan Sebelum Sesi
* Pemeriksaan Dasar
* Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Gambar Radiografi Sedang Diproses
* Hasil Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Laporan Dokter
* Riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Detail Sesi Foto Radiografi
* Rekomendasi Tindak Lanjut
* Atur Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang

Avoid member-facing titles such as:

* Pemeriksaan Pasien
* Diagnosis Saya
* Riwayat Penyakit
* Kasus Saya
* Hasil Abnormal

## Empty-state conventions

An empty state should explain:

1. what is absent;
2. why that may be expected; and
3. what the member can do next.

### No session

Message:

“Belum ada Sesi Foto Radiografi yang tercatat.”

Action:

“Jadwalkan Sesi Foto Radiografi”

### No result yet

Message:

“Hasil belum tersedia. Gambar radiografi masih diproses atau sedang ditinjau.”

Action:

“Lihat Status Sesi”

### No upcoming schedule

Message:

“Belum ada Sesi Foto Radiografi yang dijadwalkan.”

Action:

“Pilih Jadwal”

### No doctor report

Message:

“Laporan dokter belum tersedia untuk sesi ini.”

Do not imply illness or failure in empty states.

## Notification conventions

Notifications must be:

* specific;
* actionable;
* time-aware;
* proportionate to urgency; and
* privacy-conscious.

Approved examples:

* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Anda dijadwalkan pada 6 Agustus 2026 pukul 10.00.”
* “Persiapan sesi Anda belum lengkap.”
* “Pemeriksaan Dasar Anda telah selesai.”
* “Gambar radiografi sedang diproses.”
* “Hasil Sesi Foto Radiografi Anda sudah tersedia.”
* “Laporan dokter sudah tersedia.”
* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang diperlukan. Silakan pilih jadwal baru.”
* “Ada rekomendasi tindak lanjut pada hasil Anda.”

For lock-screen notifications, email subjects, SMS, and push notifications, do not expose sensitive clinical findings.

Preferred:

“Pembaruan hasil MHCS tersedia.”

Avoid:

“Hasil foto paru-paru Anda menunjukkan kelainan.”

Sensitive details should appear only after secure authentication.

## Error-message conventions

Error messages must state:

1. what failed;
2. whether user data was saved;
3. what the member should do next; and
4. whether assistance is available.

Preferred:

“Jadwal belum berhasil disimpan. Pilihan Anda tidak berubah. Silakan coba kembali.”

“Dokumen belum berhasil diunggah. Pastikan format dan ukuran file sesuai.”

“Kami belum dapat menampilkan hasil saat ini. Data Anda tetap tersimpan.”

Avoid:

* Terjadi kesalahan.
* Error 500.
* Invalid input.
* Request failed.
* Something went wrong.

A technical reference may be shown separately when useful for support.

## Confirmation-message conventions

A confirmation must identify what was completed.

Preferred:

* “Jadwal Sesi Foto Radiografi berhasil dikonfirmasi.”
* “Persiapan sesi telah disimpan.”
* “Persetujuan Anda telah tercatat.”
* “Dokumen berhasil diunggah.”
* “Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang berhasil dijadwalkan.”

Avoid generic confirmation text such as:

* Success
* Berhasil
* Data saved

without naming the completed action.

## Date and time conventions

Use explicit Indonesian date and time formats.

Preferred:

* 6 Agustus 2026
* 6 Agustus 2026 pukul 10.00
* Senin, 6 Agustus 2026
* 10.00 WITA, when the time zone must be explicit

Avoid ambiguous numeric-only dates such as:

* 06/08/26
* 08/06/26

Use the applicable site time zone where relevant.

## Capitalization and punctuation

Use sentence case for:

* body copy;
* instructions;
* notifications;
* validation messages;
* error messages;
* confirmation sentences; and
* other complete sentences.

The approved product and stage names **Sesi Foto Radiografi** and **Pemeriksaan Dasar** may use title case in:

* page titles;
* navigation labels;
* card titles;
* status labels;
* short interface elements; and
* buttons

when consistent with the approved design.

Examples:

* “Gambar radiografi sedang diproses.”
* “Jadwalkan Sesi Foto Radiografi”
* “Riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi”
* “Pemeriksaan Dasar Selesai”

Use uppercase only for the approved public queue destinations:

* `PEMERIKSAAN DASAR`
* `SESI FOTO RADIOGRAFI`

Do not use uppercase solely to create urgency.

Use punctuation for complete sentences.

Do not add periods to short button labels.

Avoid excessive exclamation marks.

## Accessibility and comprehension

Member-facing content should be understandable without specialist medical knowledge.

Rules:

* prefer familiar Indonesian words;
* explain necessary technical terms;
* use focused sentences;
* avoid unnecessary abbreviations;
* do not rely on color alone;
* pair icons with text;
* use meaningful link labels;
* state who is acting;
* state what happens next;
* distinguish recommendations from requirements;
* make dates and times explicit; and
* avoid ambiguous pronouns.

Preferred:

“Dokter menyarankan Sesi Foto Radiografi Ulang agar gambar dapat dinilai dengan lebih jelas.”

Avoid:

“Disarankan untuk mengulangnya.”

## Doctor-facing and operator-facing boundary

This document primarily governs member-facing and publicly visible content.

Doctor-facing and internal operator-facing interfaces may use precise professional terminology where it improves safety and operational clarity.

Internal terms may include:

* examination;
* imaging study;
* clinical indication;
* diagnostic report;
* findings;
* impression;
* claim;
* repeat request;
* quality decision;
* modality;
* DICOM;
* FHIR;
* worklist;
* accession;
* audit event; and
* X-ray.

Do not force member-friendly wording into professional workflows when it would reduce precision.

Any portion of an operator screen directly shown to a member must follow this member-facing policy.

## Artificial intelligence and automation language

When AI or automation contributes to member-visible content, do not imply unsupported clinical authority.

Use labels such as:

* Ringkasan Otomatis
* Penjelasan Otomatis
* Bantuan Interpretasi
* Belum Ditinjau Dokter

Do not use:

* Dokter AI
* Diagnosis AI
* Hasil Pasti dari AI
* AI Memastikan Anda Sehat

unless those claims are legally, clinically, and technically supported.

Automated member summaries must not:

* override the signed doctor report;
* invent findings;
* remove uncertainty;
* create urgency absent from the source;
* remove urgency present in the source;
* recommend unsupported treatment;
* claim doctor review that did not occur; or
* present a preliminary result as final.

## Marketing-language boundary

Marketing content may emphasize:

* accessibility;
* convenient scheduling;
* structured radiography history;
* professional handling;
* secure access;
* continuity;
* clear results; and
* informed next steps.

Marketing must not claim:

* guaranteed prevention;
* guaranteed early detection;
* complete-body certainty;
* guaranteed diagnosis;
* zero radiation risk;
* replacement of professional consultation;
* universal suitability; or
* guaranteed peace of mind.

Acceptable positioning:

“Pantau perubahan melalui riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi yang tersusun.”

Acceptable positioning:

“Pantau tubuh. Simpan riwayat. Pahami perubahannya.”

Any public claim must remain consistent with actual implemented capability.

## Examples

### Dashboard introduction

Preferred:

“Kelola jadwal, lihat riwayat Sesi Foto Radiografi, dan akses hasil Anda.”

Avoid:

“Kelola pemeriksaan dan diagnosis penyakit Anda.”

### New-session card

Preferred:

“Jadwalkan Sesi Foto Radiografi baru untuk menambahkan hasil ke riwayat Anda.”

Avoid:

“Buat pemeriksaan medis baru.”

### Queue display

Preferred:

* PEMERIKSAAN DASAR
* SESI FOTO RADIOGRAFI

Avoid:

* BASIC EXAMINATION
* X-RAY
* RADIOLOGY EXAM

### Image processing

Preferred:

“Gambar radiografi sedang diproses.”

Avoid:

“X-ray sedang diproses.”

### Result available

Preferred:

“Hasil Sesi Foto Radiografi Anda sudah tersedia.”

Avoid:

“Diagnosis baru telah keluar.”

### No immediate concern

Preferred:

“Tidak ada catatan yang memerlukan tindak lanjut segera pada sesi ini.”

Avoid:

“Anda sehat dan bebas penyakit.”

### Follow-up

Preferred:

“Dokter menyarankan tindak lanjut. Buka hasil untuk membaca penjelasan lengkap.”

Avoid:

“Hasil Anda bermasalah.”

### Repeat session

Preferred:

“Sebagian gambar radiografi perlu diambil kembali agar dapat ditinjau dengan baik.”

Avoid:

“Pemeriksaan Anda gagal.”

### Safety explanation

Preferred:

“Sesi Foto Radiografi menggunakan radiasi pengion untuk menghasilkan gambar pada bagian tubuh yang dipilih.”

Avoid:

“Foto tubuh dilakukan menggunakan teknologi yang aman tanpa risiko.”

## UI-copy review procedure

When creating or reviewing member-facing UI copy:

1. Identify whether the surface is member-facing, public, professional, regulated, internal, or mixed.
2. Confirm that MHCS-authored member-facing text is written in Bahasa Indonesia.
3. Use **Sesi Foto Radiografi** for the radiography service.
4. Use **Foto Radiografi** for member-visible radiographic results.
5. Use **Gambar Radiografi** for processing and quality contexts.
6. Preserve **Pemeriksaan Dasar** as the approved initial-stage name.
7. Confirm that MHCS-authored copy does not expose the term **X-ray** to members or the public.
8. Preserve signed, regulated, legal, clinical, or third-party text that must remain unchanged.
9. Preserve formal clinical terminology where accuracy requires it.
10. Confirm that ionizing radiation and relevant safety information remain transparent.
11. Check that no absolute health guarantee is implied.
12. Confirm that visible statuses match actual domain states.
13. Distinguish recommended and required actions.
14. Confirm that urgency is neither hidden nor exaggerated.
15. Check privacy exposure in notifications and public displays.
16. Ensure that the next action is clear.
17. Compare visible copy with backend meaning.
18. Review the rendered interface for truncation, hierarchy, and ambiguity.
19. Record intentional exceptions in implementation or review notes.

## Repository search guidance

When auditing existing copy, search for terms including:

* pasien;
* patient;
* pemeriksaan;
* medical history;
* riwayat medis;
* X-ray;
* xray;
* diagnosis;
* abnormal;
* normal;
* penyakit;
* kasus;
* case;
* gagal;
* tidak layak;
* bebas penyakit;
* sehat sepenuhnya;
* aman;
* diagnostic;
* examination;
* repeat;
* result; and
* report.

A matching occurrence is not automatically wrong.

Classify each occurrence as:

* member-facing;
* public;
* operator-facing;
* doctor-facing;
* backend or domain;
* audit;
* consent;
* formal report;
* interoperability;
* test fixture;
* third-party content; or
* documentation.

Apply this policy only to MHCS-authored member-facing and public occurrences unless another approved requirement explicitly expands the scope.

## Acceptance checklist

Member-facing UI copy is acceptable only when:

* [ ] The audience and surface type are correctly identified.
* [ ] MHCS-authored member-facing and public text is written in Bahasa Indonesia.
* [ ] The primary service term is “Sesi Foto Radiografi”.
* [ ] “Foto Radiografi” is used for member-visible radiographic results.
* [ ] “Gambar Radiografi” is used for processing and quality contexts.
* [ ] “Pemeriksaan Dasar” is preserved where applicable.
* [ ] MHCS-authored member and public copy does not use the term “X-ray”.
* [ ] Formal, signed, regulated, legal, or required third-party text remains unchanged.
* [ ] The public queue uses “PEMERIKSAAN DASAR” and “SESI FOTO RADIOGRAFI”.
* [ ] Member language is neutral and non-judgmental.
* [ ] The use of ionizing radiation is not concealed.
* [ ] Professional review is represented accurately.
* [ ] Formal clinical text remains authoritative.
* [ ] No absolute health claim is made.
* [ ] No unsupported diagnostic claim is made.
* [ ] Required and recommended actions are clearly distinguished.
* [ ] Urgent information remains explicit.
* [ ] Consent and safety language remains complete.
* [ ] Repeat-session language does not blame the member.
* [ ] Status labels match actual domain states.
* [ ] Notifications protect sensitive information.
* [ ] Buttons describe their actions.
* [ ] Empty states explain the next step.
* [ ] Errors explain recovery.
* [ ] Indonesian wording is natural and understandable.
* [ ] Broader health-history data is not mislabeled as radiography-session history.
* [ ] Backend terminology has not been renamed solely for marketing consistency.
* [ ] Any intentional exception is documented.

## Authority and conflict resolution

This document is authoritative for MHCS-authored member-facing and publicly visible language.

It does not override:

* explicit legal requirements;
* approved clinical terminology;
* signed doctor reports;
* regulated consent;
* safety requirements;
* audit requirements;
* interoperability standards;
* backend domain meaning;
* module architecture;
* approved business rules;
* required third-party text; or
* higher-priority repository instructions.

When this policy conflicts with a legal, clinical, safety, or interoperability requirement:

1. preserve the more precise requirement;
2. preserve content that must remain verbatim;
3. provide a separate plain-language Bahasa Indonesia explanation where permitted;
4. do not remove material information;
5. do not invent a compromise that changes meaning; and
6. report the conflict for review.

When no approved term exists, choose language that is:

* written in natural Bahasa Indonesia;
* neutral;
* preventive;
* accurate;
* transparent;
* calm;
* non-judgmental;
* understandable to a general audience; and
* consistent with the underlying domain state.
